android-patterns|Confirmation.summary: A Plenix confirmation on Android asks before an action that others will see or that cannot come back, and offers Undo instead for what can. The question is the Plenix alert dialog (Material 3’s dialog with the Plenix look): the title names the action and the count (“Delete 2 categories?”), the body says the consequence and lists what goes, and the confirm button says the verb, in the danger colors when it destroys. Focus starts on Cancel. Type to confirm adds a text field for the item’s name. Reversible actions skip the question and show a Snackbar with Undo.

anatomy.about: The title names the verb and the count, or the item by its name.

anatomy.about: One sentence on what else is lost or kept, then “This cannot be undone.”

anatomy.about: Up to five of the items, then “and N more”, in the body.

anatomy.about: Cancel first, then the verb; the verb in the danger colors when it destroys.

anatomy.name: Snackbar
anatomy.about: The result with Undo, for actions that can be reversed.

compose: // the Plenix confirmation: the question with the count, the consequence, the names, Cancel first, the verb last
fun PlenixConfirm(title: String, message: String, names: List<String>, confirmLabel: String, destructive: Boolean,
names.take(5).forEach { Text(it, color = PlenixColors.contentDefault.current(), fontSize = PlenixPlatform.textBodySize) }
if (names.size > 5) Text("and ${names.size - 5} more", color = PlenixColors.contentMuted.current(), fontSize = PlenixPlatform.textSecondarySize)
views: .setMessage("Their assets stay, without these categories. This cannot be undone.")
